_comment: THIRD-PARTY VENDORED SOURCE. This directory is not ours. It is the published
ScaleformUI_Lua.zip from upstream release 5.8.1, extracted whole, plus the two
local patches listed below and nothing else -- no reformatting, no
restructuring, no 'improvements'. Every byte outside the two BR-PATCH blocks --
one in fxmanifest.lua, one in ScaleformUI.lua -- is byte-identical to that
release asset, whose sha256 is recorded in `release_assets` below, so the next
upstream bump is: download the new ScaleformUI_Lua.zip, extract it over this
directory, then re-apply the patches. Keeping that true is the whole reason
tools/verify.sh reads this file. The `vendored third-party` gate checks that
the LICENSE is present, that every BR-PATCH marker in the tree is declared
here and every patch declared here is present in the tree, and that
tools/deploy.sh actually syncs this resource to the box -- because shipping
a resource that never reaches the server is a failure mode this project has
THIS RESOURCE DOES NOT WORK ALONE. It needs ScaleformUI_Assets, its sibling in
this group, which streams the compiled .gfx movies it requests at start. See
license_note: NOT MIT, unlike the other vendored resource in this repository, so the terms
are different in a way that matters: attribution is required, derivatives
must be shared alike, and COMMERCIAL USE IS NOT PERMITTED. Upstream's README
says the same thing in its own words -- use it in your resources freely, but
you cannot ship it inside a paid resource.
The owner considered this and decided on 2026-09-08 that our use fits within
CC BY-NC-SA. That decision is his to make and is recorded here so the next
person does not have to re-litigate it; it is NOT a lawyer's opinion and it
would need revisiting if this server ever sells anything that includes this
The upstream repository keeps its notice at the REPOSITORY ROOT as
LICENSE.txt, and neither release zip contains it. So LICENSE here is an ADDED
file: a verbatim copy of that LICENSE.txt, renamed to LICENSE because CC
requires the notice to travel with the code and because verify.sh looks for
that exact name. It is the only file in this directory that did not come out

why: Upstream's README states it outright: 'This also requires an Assets resource
from the Github Repo Releases, it will not work without them.' The assets
resource streams the compiled Flash movies (.gfx) that this library requests
by name at start -- ScaleformUI, ScaleformUIPause, PauseMenuHeader,
RadialMenu, RadioMenu -- and owns the minimap overlay loader that
Without it the library starts, sits waiting for movies that never load, and
hard_dependency.start_order: ensure ScaleformUI_Assets BEFORE ScaleformUI_Lua, so the streamed .gfx are registered before this resource's start-up thread requests them.

provenance_check.claim: This directory is the extracted ScaleformUI_Lua.zip of release 5.8.1, and that zip's ScaleformUI.lua is not an opaque build artifact -- it is the tag's own source, concatenated. All 125 .lua files under ScaleformUI_Lua/src/ at tag 5.8.1 appear in it verbatim, in case-insensitive path order, separated by a 73-character banner comment. Nothing is added and nothing is removed: the 9,124 characters by which the bundle exceeds the sum of its sources are exactly those 125 banners.
provenance_check.claim_is_as_vendored: That claim describes this directory as it was vendored, at commit 731c5d0. BR-PATCH 2 has since edited ScaleformUI.lua -- one comment block and three lines of code inside the MinimapOverlays thread, and nothing else in the file. Re-running the check today means allowing for that one block; every other byte of the bundle is still the release asset.
how: sha256sum ScaleformUI_Lua.zip   # must equal release_assets below
git clone https://github.com/manups4e/ScaleformUI.git && git -C ScaleformUI archive 5.8.1 ScaleformUI_Lua | tar -x
# then, for each src/**/*.lua at the tag, assert its whitespace-normalised body
# occurs in the released ScaleformUI.lua, and that the order of first occurrence
# equals the case-insensitive sort of the source paths.
provenance_check.note: Compare the ZIP by sha256, not the extracted worktree. This repository's .gitattributes normalises text to LF, so a checked-out ScaleformUI.lua on Windows may hold CRLF and will not hash like the zip member -- that is a property of your core.autocrlf setting, not of the code. The .gfx files in the sibling assets resource are pinned `binary` in .gitattributes for the same reason, where the stakes are higher: a substituted CR inside a compiled Flash movie is silent corruption no gate here would catch.

why_vendored: The owner evaluated upstream's demo menu on 2026-09-08 and wanted this look:
'feels exactly like Rockstar's'. It is vendored rather than installed by hand
for the reason every third-party resource here is -- tools/deploy.sh syncs what
is in this repository and nothing else, so a hand-installed copy is a version
nobody can see from the commit history and nobody can reproduce on a new box.
The CHOICE OF THE RELEASE ZIP over the repository's src/ tree was deliberate.
The alternative was vendoring ScaleformUI_Lua/src/ from tag 5.8.1 -- 125 files
loaded by the manifest's 'src/**/*.lua' glob, which is how upstream develops.
It lost on two counts. First, the .gfx assets only exist as a release artifact,
so pairing the library with the same release removes any chance of version
skew between the Lua and the movies it drives. Second, the glob form makes
load order a property of FiveM's glob expansion, and this library defines
classes by file-scope inheritance, where a wrong order is a nil __index at
start. The bundle has one fixed order. Nothing was given up by choosing it:
the check above proves the bundle IS those 125 files, in that order.

patches.what: Commented out the 'example.lua' entry. The file itself is left in place, unmodified.
patches.why: example.lua is upstream's showcase demo and it is not inert: loaded, it draws a green world marker at the player's spawn, adds two timer bars, types 'this is a test' onto the minimap four seconds after start, and then runs a forever loop watching for demo hotkeys. This round vendors the library and proves it starts; it writes no menus and changes no gameplay, and a stranger's demo UI on every player's screen is the opposite of that. Kept rather than deleted so the demo the owner actually evaluated stays one uncomment away.
patches.upstream_fixable: not a bug -- the manifest line directly above it invites exactly this change: 'You can comment example.lua if you don't need it!'

patches.what: That thread's else branch was a bare MinimapOverlays:Load() and it ran on EVERY FRAME. It now calls Load() only while MinimapOverlays.overlay is still 0, and the branch waits 500ms per pass, so the thread stops working as soon as the overlay handle arrives. Three lines of code. Load() itself, isLoaded, the cursor-selection branch above it and everything else in this 20,000-line file are untouched.
patches.why: isLoaded is assigned, at the end of Load(), as HasMinimapOverlayLoaded(overlay) and HasScaleformMovieLoaded(minimapHandle). minimapHandle is initialized to 0 and the block that would set it is COMMENTED OUT UPSTREAM at the top of Load(), so HasScaleformMovieLoaded(0) is false, isLoaded can never become true, and the else branch never stopped: one cross-resource TriggerEvent('ScUI:AddMinimapOverlay') into ScaleformUI_Assets plus a SetMinimapOverlayDisplay, every frame, for the whole session, whether or not any menu or overlay existed. That is precisely the shape the framerate investigation immediately before this vendoring landed on -- cheap Lua dispatching engine and event work, which the resource profiler bills to nobody -- so importing it was not acceptable. NOTHING IS LOST BY STOPPING: initializeScaleforms() already calls Load() once at start, and every Add*OverlayToMap calls it when overlay == 0, so a caller that legitimately wants an overlay still gets one. The retry itself is kept because that is what the branch is for -- if ScaleformUI_Assets has not registered its handler yet, the first Load() reaches nobody and the handle stays 0 -- it just stops once it has succeeded.
patches.what_was_deliberately_not_done: isLoaded was not 'repaired'. Dropping the minimapHandle term from it would send the thread down the branch above instead, calling GetScaleformMovieCursorSelection(0) every frame -- the same fault wearing a different hat. Uncommenting upstream's handle acquisition was the other option and it is worse: it requests a second 'minimap' scaleform and toggles SetBigmapActive on and then off at start, on every client, for a mouse-event feature no menu of ours uses.
patches.upstream_fixable: yes -- an unconditional per-frame Load() in a retry branch would be accepted upstream as a bug fix. The deeper fix is upstream's alone: restore minimapHandle (the commented block at the top of Load()), without which the cursor-selection half of this thread is dead code.
patches.recheck_at_next_bump: Look at the else branch of that thread. If upstream has made isLoaded reachable -- i.e. minimapHandle is set again -- this patch is no longer load-bearing, though it stays harmless: the branch is then simply not taken. If the branch is still an unconditional Load(), re-apply. The cursor polling resumes on its own within 500ms of isLoaded turning true, so keeping the patch does not block an upstream fix.

untouched_on_purpose: ScaleformUI.lua -- the library itself, one patch (BR-PATCH 2) and nothing else. Of the two upstream faults reported at vendoring time, the first -- MinimapOverlays:Load() called every frame forever, because minimapHandle stays 0 and isLoaded therefore never turns true -- is the one the owner asked to have fixed, and BR-PATCH 2 is that fix.

The second fault stands, on purpose. THIS LIBRARY RUNS ALWAYS-ON THREADS FROM RESOURCE START, whether or not any menu exists: the main one, below initializeScaleforms(), loops at Citizen.Wait(0) calling Warning:Update(), InstructionalButtons:Update(), BigMessageInstance:Update() and five more on every frame, and a third ticks GlobalGameTimer every 100ms. BR-PATCH 2 idles the minimap thread and that is as far as it goes without restructuring upstream's start-up, which is a rewrite rather than a patch. If ScaleformUI ever shows up in a framerate investigation, that main thread is where to look first.
example.lua -- byte-identical to the release. Only its manifest entry is commented out.

COLORS. The owner asked for 'our colors for now'. Nothing was recolored here and that is not an omission: ScaleformUI takes its colors per menu at construction time (SColor.HUD_Yellow and friends, passed when a UIMenu is built), so there is no palette inside the library to change. Our colors get applied by the code that builds our menus, which this round deliberately does not write.
